clinician.trajectory_summary: A female market worker in her 50s presented with 6 months of fingertip pain and swelling. Physical examination revealed mild clubbing of both thumbs and index fingers. Radiography and MRI confirmed band acro-osteolysis of the distal phalanges of both thumbs and index fingers, with a destructive change in the DIP joint of the right middle finger. Laboratory tests showed no elevations in C-reactive protein, serum alkaline phosphatase, calcium, or intact parathyroid hormone. Serum was negative for rheumatoid factor, anti-DNA antibodies, anti-Scl-70 antibody, and anticentromere antibodies. Psoriatic arthritis was considered but deemed unlikely as the patient did not meet CASPAR criteria, lacking personal or family history of psoriasis, typical psoriatic nail changes, or current/past dactylitis. The patient also had no history of Raynaud’s phenomenon, traumatic hand injury, frostbite, or exposure to polyvinyl chloride, nor a family history of congenital bone dysplasia or psoriasis. The extensive workup ruling out common causes supports an idiopathic etiology.
